summary: Most travelers praise the Osprey Farpoint 40 Travel Pack for a hip-belt harness that carries weight comfortably and for build quality that lasts for years. Its weak points are the bottle pockets and laptop sleeve, which many find awkward or useless when packed. A minority find it uncomfortable, heavy or bulky.

Many travelers like the Peak Design Travel Backpack 45L for its organization, durability and camera-friendly layout, but the most common verdict is that it is heavy and the thin shoulder straps are uncomfortable under load. Some also report straps, sternum strap or snaps failing. It suits airport-to-hotel carrying and gear-heavy trips better than long walks.

Travelers like the Cotopaxi Allpa 35L Travel Pack for its clamshell opening, organization, durable fabric and carry-on size. The main complaints are comfort, with straps and hip belt that suit some frames poorly, especially shorter torsos, plus a bulky, floppy look when not full and some heaviness. A few report the exterior coating peeling.

The Aer Travel Pack 3 is praised for solid build, a comfortable harness and strong organization, particularly for people carrying a laptop and tech. The main complaint is weight, followed by a laptop section and pockets that eat into the main compartment so it holds less than its size suggests. Some also find it pricey.

The Osprey Fairview 40 Travel Pack is most often described as very comfortable, with a frame, hip belt and stowable straps that carry weight well, including for smaller and shorter-torso travelers. Some find it too big or heavy for budget-airline limits, and a minority find the straps uncomfortable. Bottle pockets and the laptop sleeve draw criticism.

Travelers like the Aer Travel Pack 3 Small for its comfortable harness, organization and fit under many airline seats. The main complaints are weight and a stiff, bulky build whose padding and pockets eat capacity, so it holds less than its size suggests. It suits people carrying tech more than those wanting a light or roomy bag.

Travelers like the Cotopaxi Allpa 28L Travel Pack as a personal-item-size bag with a clamshell layout and plenty of organization. Comfort is the main complaint, as some find it tiring or painful after a short time, especially when full. Travelers also note no bottle pocket and zippers that strain when packed tightly.

Travelers like the Patagonia Black Hole Mini MLC Pack 30L for being light, roomy and comfortable, with one big compartment that often passes as a personal item. The main complaint is thin straps and little support under heavy loads. Some find the laptop section eats space or that it runs long for strict airline sizers.

Travelers like the Peak Design Packing Cube for tough, stretchy fabric, good compression and a handy dirty-clothes section, and many say it holds up well over time. Some find it pricey or heavier than cheaper cubes, and a few say the zipper creeps open when overstuffed.

Most travelers of the Matador 35L Global Travel Pack like the comfortable hip-belt harness, materials and pockets. Weight and bulk are the main reasons some returned it, and the hip belt is widely called hard to remove. A few mention stitching or quality problems, and some find it tall for under a seat.

Travelers like the Cotopaxi Allpa 42L Travel Pack for organization, a clamshell opening and usually getting through carry-on checks. Its main drawbacks are weight and comfort when full, since it lacks a frame and is easy to overpack. Some find it too big, floppy or hard to fit in small overhead bins.

Travelers like the Peak Design Travel Backpack 30L for its looks, durability and a size that often fits under the seat. The most common complaint is uncomfortable, thin shoulder straps, along with some weight. Interior pockets and organization are described as awkward by several travelers. A hip belt helps some.

The Minaal Carry-on 3.0 is praised for durability, a comfortable harness with load lifters, a sleek look and a protected laptop compartment. Downsides are some weight, a poor bottle pocket and an unstructured main space that some find awkward to pack without cubes. Several also feel the price is high.

Travelers of the Matador 45L Global Travel Pack mostly like the harness, build and organization, and many say it carries heavy loads well. The common drawbacks are that it is heavy and large, with stiff zippers and a tight laptop compartment. A few report stitching or strap fraying problems.

Travelers like the Osprey Farpoint 55 Travel Pack for a comfortable harness with a useful hip belt and a detachable daypack that many use as their under-seat bag. It is large, and several note it only just passes as a carry-on or is better downsized. A few find it uncomfortable or awkward to pack.

Travelers praise the Tom Bihn Synik 30 for organization, build quality and a laptop compartment, and most find it comfortable. Some find it too small for trips with extra shoes or a few days of clothes, and a few find it hard to pack or heavy. The price is mentioned as steep. It suits everyday carry and short trips.

Travelers praise the Tom Bihn Aeronaut 30 for tough, long-lasting construction, a big flexible main compartment and fitting under most seats. It behaves more like a duffel than a backpack, so the straps can be uncomfortable for longer carries and it suits travelers without a laptop best.

Travelers like the Away The Bigger Carry-On for sturdy build, smooth wheels and fitting overhead bins on most flights. Several found it too large for some cheap European airlines or small planes and had to check it. It is easy to overload, and a few report zipper or handle failures that were replaced.

Travelers praise the Tom Bihn Aeronaut 45 for very durable construction, flexible carry modes and fitting carry-on limits, including on regional jets. The main drawbacks are weight when full and straps that some find uncomfortable as a backpack, so it works better with the duffel strap.

Travelers mostly describe the Osprey Sojourn Porter 30L Travel Pack as comfortable, with a hip belt and stowable straps, and many say it fits under a seat. Some find the padding, rigid panels and compression system eat capacity and slow packing and access, and the bottle sleeve and laptop pocket draw complaints.

Most travelers find the Eagle Creek Tour Travel Pack 40L comfortable thanks to an adjustable harness and a hip belt that tucks away, and call it light and low-key for a 40L carry-on. A couple found the hip belt or straps uncomfortable and returned it, and a few note the padding and rain cover eat into space.

Most travelers report the Away Carry-On lasting for years of frequent travel, with wheels and shell holding up and scuffs the usual wear. It generally passes overhead bin checks, though a few say it holds little for its weight, one saw a cracked shell within months, and one was charged at a budget airline for size.

Many travelers have used the Tom Bihn Synapse 25 for years, some for ten or more, and call it hard-wearing, roomy and well organized for everyday carry and one-bag trips. Fit is the main drawback: a few found it hung low or ran too long for a short torso, while strap adjustment and the frame sheet helped others.

Most travelers find the Able Carry Max comfortable even fully loaded, with strong organization and a sleek look that suits work trips and short one-bag travel. The main downsides are its weight and limited capacity, plus some scuffing and crinkly noise from the X-Pac fabric.

Most travelers find the Tortuga Pro Backpack 40L very comfortable even fully packed, with a strong harness and hip belt and sturdy build. Weight is the main downside, and some find the padding bulky. Fit can be an issue for short torsos, and a few miss external lash points.

Many travelers like the Osprey Fairview 55 for its roomy main pack, adjustable fit and detachable daypack, and several found it comfortable, including shorter travelers. The main downsides are size and weight when fully packed, and some doubt it passes as a carry-on if overfilled.

Many travelers describe the Osprey Sojourn Porter 46L as a durable, flexible bag with strong compression and many pockets, used for years of flights with few gate problems. Comfort is split: some call it very comfortable with a good hip belt, while several found it uncomfortable for long wear.

Travelers are highly positive about the Tom Bihn Techonaut 30, calling it comfortable, easy to organize and surprisingly roomy for a bag that fits under the seat. A few nitpicks appear, such as an exposed main zipper and dangling straps, and one found it too small for a three-day trip.

Travelers are divided on the Peak Design Everyday Backpack 20L. Fans praise its looks, side access and durability for daily carry, while a notable group found it uncomfortable, citing thin straps and a rigid back panel. Some also found it boxy or built more around camera gear than general use.

Most travelers praise the GORUCK GR2 34L as tough, well built and good at carrying heavy loads, with plush straps and solid organization. Downsides are comfort for some, with a back panel that makes them sweat or too little padding, plus a tight laptop compartment and a military look.

Travelers like the Patagonia Black Hole Pack 32L for being light, with big pockets, a roomy top lid compartment and a size that suits overhead bins. Downsides include no hip belt, shoulder straps that dig when heavily loaded, and a single open main compartment that needs packing cubes.

Most travelers find the Tortuga Lite Backpack 40L comfortable and light, with plenty of space and a simple layout. Some quibbles recur around fit: a few say it sits low or pulls back when loaded, and a couple call the hip belt minimal or feel it is small for 40L.

Travelers like the Cotopaxi Allpa Mini 20L as a small, comfortable pack that opens fully and fits personal item limits, including for shorter travelers. It suits weekend trips well. The tablet pocket is too small for some, and a few wish it had the bigger Allpa's extra organization.

Travelers are very positive about the Tom Bihn Synik 22, praising its build quality, straps and clamshell organization for everyday carry and light one-bag trips. The main downsides are tight space on longer trips and some wishing it were lighter or that they had chosen the larger size.

Travelers see the Matador 18L Personal Item Travel Pack as a small, light pack that fits under seats and suits a daypack or a short trip of a couple of days. Several find it tiny, and a few say it works better for everyday carry than travel.

Travelers like the Tom Bihn Synapse 19 as a durable, well-organized everyday and commuter bag that handles short trips and fits smaller frames. Its size is the main limit: a few find it too small for one-bag travel or a laptop, and one found it uncomfortable to wear.

Most travelers find the Aer Travel Pack 4 28L very comfortable, with supportive straps, load lifters and a hip belt that handle a full load. Space is the main caveat, as a couple say it offers little more room than smaller packs, and its under-seat fit is debated.
